questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Attractiveness of the city/country, quality of education on host university, grant/financial support opportunities, concerns over COVID cases and restrictions

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the student exchange staff was quite helpful and quickly replied to emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a welcoming session for Erasmus+ students in which we could pose questions and receive helpful information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Despite not personally having experienced that, there seems to be a problem in terms of housing availability, therefore it can be difficult for incoming students to find housing. I would recommend looking for housing in as many different platforms as possible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be hard to find housing, but on the positive side Wageningen is a small town, so even the housing further from University is still not very far.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On the university website for incoming students there is information on which courses are available for exchange students to take. After admission to Wageningen University, we can already register for all the courses that we will be taking, and we have available information on how to do so.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of information available on the university website, and if needed the exchange students office is quick to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not have any problem registering to my chosen courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is plenty of information available for incoming students to make an informed decision, and the university student office is ready to help if we need so.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses tend to demand a high amount of work, since usually there is pre-class work to read or prepare, and assignments to do.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses are in my opinion more interactive, the students are required to participate and engage more. The classes time is more balanced,

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Impact assessment of Policies and Programs, The origins of global economic inequality, policy projects and programs for development, law and political power, international economics: trade and development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed every course that I took. The professors were knowledgeable and the course structure was nicely organised

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Since the Wageningen is quite small, it is common to visit other cities. Public transportation can be quite expensive at times.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation was more expensive than what I was expecting

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We have available a wide variety of sports for a very low price (at the university gym), and Wageningen as an active student life with student organizations and private people creating events and get-togethers

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are whatsapp and facebook groups that announce events in which there is opportunity to meet other students and have a nice leasure time

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The Netherlands is easy to travel by train, so there are many cities available for a one day or weekend trip. It is also easy to go to Germany, Luxemburg, Belgium and even Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Wageningen is a University city

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join as many events as possible especially in the first weeks of the semester when new students are meeting eachother

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Comparing to Denmark, the culture is very similar, I would think.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The willingness to have a nice university-social life balance, and to get together for a dinner or coffee

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: There will be plenty of University work (not the stereotypical "Erasmus" experience), the international environment is very diverse and interesting, the university schedule tends to allow you the freedom to plan many leisure activities throughout the week

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join facebook groups (for example, Wageningen Student Plaza) to get help or information from other students

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting different students, experiencing an alternative education style, being introduced to new knowledge, travelling around

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The weather in The Netherlands can be quite gloomy - even if it is not very cold, or even when it is not raining, there are a lot of days in which the sky is grey from sunrise to sunset

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
